Objectives

Estimand Summary

To demonstrate that Drug A is superior to Drug B in prolonging PFS in participants with previously untreated, PD-L1-positive (TPS ≥1%), locally advanced or metastatic NSCLC

Population: Participants with previously untreated, PD-L1-positive (TPS ≥1%), locally advanced or metastatic NSCLC without actionable genomic alterations, as defined by the eligibility criteria (Section 5.1); analyzed in the full analysis set (FAS) Treatment: Drug A 20 mg/kg IV Q3W vs Drug B 200 mg IV Q3W, each for up to 35 cycles Endpoint: PFS, defined as the time from randomization to the first documented disease progression per Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors version 1.1 (RECIST v1.1) as assessed by blinded independent central review (BICR), or death from any cause, whichever occurs first Summary: Hazard ratio (HR) for Drug A vs Drug B from a stratified Cox proportional hazards model; median PFS by Kaplan-Meier method Population: Participants with previously untreated, PD-L1-positive (TPS ≥1%), locally advanced or metastatic NSCLC without actionable genomic alterations, as defined by the eligibility criteria (Section 5.1); analyzed in the full analysis set (FAS) Treatment: Drug A 20 mg/kg IV Q3W vs Drug B 200 mg IV Q3W, each for up to 35 cycles Endpoint: PFS, defined as the time from randomization to the first documented disease progression per Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors version 1.1 (RECIST v1.1) as assessed by blinded independent central review (BICR), or death from any cause, whichever occurs first Summary: Hazard ratio (HR) for Drug A vs Drug B from a stratified Cox proportional hazards model; median PFS by Kaplan-Meier method

Key secondary: To demonstrate that Drug A is superior to Drug B in prolonging OS

Population: As for the primary estimand (FAS) Treatment: As for the primary estimand, followed by any subsequent therapy Endpoint: OS, defined as the time from randomization to death from any cause Summary: HR from a stratified Cox proportional hazards model; median OS by Kaplan-Meier method

To compare the antitumor activity of Drug A with that of Drug B

Population: All randomized participants; participants with a confirmed CR or PR for duration of response. Treatment: Drug A 20 mg/kg IV Q3W vs Drug B 200 mg IV Q3W, each for up to 35 cycles Endpoint: ORR: proportion of participants with a confirmed complete response (CR) or partial response (PR) per RECIST v1.1 by BICR Duration of response (DoR): time from first documented CR or PR to disease progression by BICR or death PFS per RECIST v1.1 by investigator assessment PFS2: time from randomization to progression on next-line therapy or death from any cause Summary: Response proportions by treatment group; Kaplan-Meier estimates for DoR, investigator-assessed PFS, and PFS2, with hazard ratios for between-group time-to-event comparisons.

To evaluate the safety and tolerability of Drug A compared with Drug B

Population: Participants who receive study intervention. Treatment: Drug A 20 mg/kg IV Q3W vs Drug B 200 mg IV Q3W, each for up to 35 cycles Endpoint: Incidence and severity of adverse events (AEs), serious AEs (SAEs), immune-mediated AEs, and AEs of special interest (AESIs), graded per NCI-CTCAE v5.0 Incidence of clinical laboratory abnormalities, including liver chemistry elevations meeting protocol-defined liver event criteria Incidence of AEs leading to dose interruption or permanent discontinuation Summary: Numbers and proportions of participants with adverse events and clinical laboratory abnormalities, summarized by treatment group and severity.

To compare patient-reported disease-related symptoms and health-related quality of life (HRQoL)

Population: All randomized participants. Treatment: Drug A 20 mg/kg IV Q3W vs Drug B 200 mg IV Q3W, each for up to 35 cycles Endpoint: Time to deterioration (TTD) in cough, chest pain, and dyspnea (EORTC QLQ-LC13) Change from baseline in global health status/QoL (EORTC QLQ-C30) Summary: Time-to-deterioration distributions and mean change from baseline in global health status/QoL by treatment group.

To characterize the pharmacokinetics (PK) of Drug A

Population: Participants receiving Drug A with evaluable serum concentration measurements. Treatment: Drug A 20 mg/kg IV Q3W, for up to 35 cycles Endpoint: Serum concentrations of Drug A (maximum and trough concentrations) Summary: Descriptive statistics for maximum and trough serum concentrations of Drug A.

To evaluate the immunogenicity of Drug A

Population: Participants receiving Drug A with evaluable immunogenicity assessments. Treatment: Drug A 20 mg/kg IV Q3W, for up to 35 cycles Endpoint: Incidence of antidrug antibodies (ADAs) and neutralizing antibodies (NAbs) to Drug A Summary: Numbers and proportions of participants with ADAs and NAbs to Drug A.

narrativeContentItems.text: This Phase 3 study addresses the need for improved first-line treatment options for adults with PD-L1-positive advanced NSCLC. The trial rationale and supporting background are provided in Sections 2.1.1 and 2.1.2, respectively.

narrativeContentItems.name: NCI-10
narrativeContentItems.text: Drug B monotherapy is a standard first-line treatment for PD-L1-positive advanced NSCLC without actionable genomic alterations, but most patients experience disease progression within the first year. In the Phase 2 study Demo-00201, Drug A produced a median progression-free survival (PFS) of 10.2 months with a manageable safety profile, compared with approximately 6 months expected with ICI monotherapy in a similar population. This study will determine whether Drug A is superior to Drug B in prolonging PFS.

narrativeContentItems.name: NCI-11
narrativeContentItems.text: A detailed description of the chemistry, pharmacology, efficacy, and safety of Drug A is provided in the Investigator's Brochure (IB). Information on Drug B is provided in the locally approved prescribing information.

narrativeContentItems.name: NCI-12
narrativeContentItems.text: Lung cancer is the leading cause of cancer death worldwide, and NSCLC accounts for approximately 85% of cases. For patients without actionable genomic alterations, first-line options include ICI monotherapy for tumors expressing PD-L1, or immunotherapy combined with platinum-based chemotherapy (Hendriks 2023). Drug B monotherapy is approved for patients with PD-L1 tumor proportion score (TPS) ≥1% and improved overall survival (OS) compared with chemotherapy in this population. Drug B monotherapy is frequently selected for patients who prefer to avoid chemotherapy-related toxicity; however, median PFS with ICI monotherapy remains under 1 year, and most patients ultimately progress.

narrativeContentItems.name: NCI-13
narrativeContentItems.text: Drug B is the standard against which new first-line treatments for this population are judged, so a randomized superiority comparison with Drug B provides the most direct evidence of clinical benefit. Drug A shares immune checkpoint inhibition with Drug B and adds anti-angiogenic activity, which counteracts tumor immunosuppression; any improvement over Drug B can therefore be attributed to the additional activity of Drug A. Randomized evidence that adding anti-angiogenic therapy to immune checkpoint inhibition improves outcomes in NSCLC (Socinski 2018), together with the Phase 2 results for Drug A (Section 2.1.2), supports the assumed PFS hazard ratio of 0.70 (Section 10.11).

narrativeContentItems.name: NCI-14
narrativeContentItems.text: In nonclinical studies, binding of the angiogenic ligand increased the avidity of Drug A for its checkpoint target by more than 15-fold, and Drug A produced greater tumor growth inhibition in syngeneic models than an ICI alone. An Fc-silencing modification minimizes antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity and cytokine release. In the Phase 1 study Demo-00101 (N=78; 3 to 30 mg/kg every 3 weeks [Q3W]), no maximum tolerated dose was reached, and doses ≥10 mg/kg maintained >95% peripheral checkpoint receptor occupancy and complete suppression of the free angiogenic ligand at trough. In the Phase 2 study Demo-00201, 120 participants with previously untreated PD-L1-positive NSCLC received Drug A 20 mg/kg Q3W. The confirmed objective response rate (ORR) was 48% (95% confidence interval [CI]: 39% to 57%), and median PFS was 10.2 months. The terminal half-life of Drug A is approximately 7 days, and steady state is reached by Cycle 4 (Investigator’s Brochure, Section 5.1).

narrativeContentItems.name: NCI-17
narrativeContentItems.text: Participants randomized to Drug A may experience improved disease control compared with standard ICI monotherapy, based on the antitumor activity observed in Study Demo-00201. All participants will receive close monitoring, including regular tumor imaging, laboratory tests, and physician assessments, which may permit earlier detection and management of disease progression and adverse events. narrativeContentItems.name: NCI-19

Drug A is a novel, humanized, bispecific immunoglobulin G1 (IgG1) antibody that combines immune checkpoint inhibition with anti-angiogenic activity.

NCI-35
narrativeContentItems.text:
This is a Phase 3, randomized, double-blind, active-controlled, parallel-group, multicenter, global superiority study of Drug A compared with Drug B as first-line treatment for PD-L1-positive, locally advanced or metastatic NSCLC. Approximately 600 participants will be randomized at approximately 250 sites in North America, Europe, and the Asia-Pacific region (Figure 1).

  • After a screening period of up to 28 days, eligible participants will be randomized 1:1 to Drug A 20 mg/kg IV Q3W or Drug B 200 mg IV Q3W, stratified by PD-L1 TPS (1% to 49% vs ≥50%) and histology (squamous vs nonsquamous).
  • Study intervention will continue until disease progression per RECIST v1.1 by BICR, unacceptable toxicity, withdrawal of consent, or a maximum of 35 cycles (approximately 24 months). Treatment beyond progression is permitted under the conditions in Section 7.1. Crossover between arms is not permitted.
  • Participants, caregivers, investigators, site staff, BICR reviewers, and the sponsor study team will be blinded to intervention assignment (Section 6.7.3).
  • After the last dose, participants will have a safety follow-up visit 30 days later, will continue tumor imaging until progression if they stopped treatment for another reason, and will be followed for survival every 12 weeks.
  • An independent data monitoring committee (IDMC) will review unblinded safety data approximately every 6 months and the interim analysis of OS (Section 10.9, Section 11.4).

This study design includes participant, caregiver, investigator, and assessor masking.

narrativeContentItems.name: NCI-36
narrativeContentItems.text: A patient advisory board of 8 people living with lung cancer and 2 caregivers reviewed the draft design. Based on their input, the visit schedule was aligned with treatment visits to minimize additional travel, patient-reported outcome (PRO) questionnaires were limited to 2 validated instruments, and telephone contact was permitted for survival follow-up. Participants will also have the option to complete a voluntary Study Participant Feedback Questionnaire on their clinical study experience.

narrativeContentItems.name: NCI-37
narrativeContentItems.text: A randomized, double-blind, active-controlled design provides an unbiased comparison of Drug A with a guideline-recommended standard of care. Blinding is feasible because both interventions are administered intravenously on the same schedule, and it reduces bias in investigator decisions on progression, treatment continuation, and AE attribution. A maximum treatment duration of 35 cycles is consistent with the approved duration of Drug B monotherapy and applies to both arms to avoid differential exposure.

The treatment policy strategy for study intervention discontinuation allows the primary estimand to reflect the effect of randomized treatment assignment, including outcomes after treatment stops. The rationale for the hypothetical strategy for new anticancer therapy is provided in Section 3.1, and the rationale for selecting PFS and assessment by BICR is provided in Section 4.2.

For the key secondary estimand, OS captures the clinically relevant outcome of survival. Applying a treatment policy strategy to discontinuation and subsequent anticancer therapy allows the survival comparison to reflect outcomes following randomized treatment assignment across the subsequent course of care (see Section 3.2).

narrativeContentItems.name: NCI-39
narrativeContentItems.text: The randomized parallel-group intervention model described in Section 4.1 provides an unbiased comparison of Drug A with Drug B. A maximum treatment duration of 35 cycles applies to both arms to avoid differential exposure and is consistent with the approved duration of Drug B monotherapy. The rationale for intervention dose and regimen selection is provided in Section 6.2.

narrativeContentItems.name: NCI-40
narrativeContentItems.text: Drug B monotherapy is selected as the active control because it is approved and recommended by international guidelines as first-line treatment for PD-L1-positive (TPS ≥1%) advanced NSCLC without actionable genomic alterations (Hendriks 2023). Comparison with Drug B will establish whether Drug A provides clinical benefit beyond the current ICI standard of care. The rationale for the comparator dose and regimen is provided in Section 6.2.

The interim OS analysis provides an opportunity to assess evidence of an OS benefit before the final OS analysis, while controlling type I error through the Lan-DeMets alpha-spending approach with O’Brien-Fleming boundaries. Its timing at the primary PFS analysis, when approximately 170 deaths (45% information fraction) are expected, allows an initial assessment of OS alongside the primary efficacy results. OS testing is conditional on statistically significant PFS results under the hierarchical testing procedure (see Sections 10.9 and 10.10).

narrativeContentItems.name: NCI-44
narrativeContentItems.text: Drug B monotherapy is approved and recommended by international guidelines as first-line treatment for PD-L1-positive (TPS ≥1%) advanced NSCLC without actionable genomic alterations (Hendriks 2023). A superiority comparison with Drug B therefore tests whether Drug A provides clinical benefit beyond the current ICI standard of care.

narrativeContentItems.name: NCI-45
narrativeContentItems.text: PFS is an accepted primary endpoint for first-line NSCLC studies when the expected treatment effect is large and the endpoint is assessed rigorously (FDA 2018). PFS is not confounded by subsequent therapies and is expected to read out earlier than OS. Assessment by BICR minimizes measurement bias. OS is the key secondary endpoint and will be tested under strong control of the type I error rate (Section 10.10).

narrativeContentItems.name: NCI-46
narrativeContentItems.text: PD-L1 TPS ≥50% is associated with greater benefit from ICI therapy, and squamous histology is associated with a different prognosis and anti-angiogenic class-related bleeding risk. Stratification by these 2 factors maintains balance between arms for the main known prognostic and predictive factors while limiting the number of strata. Region is not a stratification factor; its effect will be explored in subgroup analyses (Section 10.8.2).

narrativeContentItems.name: NCI-52
narrativeContentItems.text: To be eligible to participate in this trial, an individual must meet all the following criteria:

narrativeContentItems.name: NCI-53
narrativeContentItems.text: 1. Participant must be 18 years of age or the legal age of consent in the jurisdiction in which the study is taking place, whichever is older, at the time of signing the informed consent.

narrativeContentItems.name: NCI-54
narrativeContentItems.text:
2. Histologically or cytologically confirmed NSCLC of squamous or nonsquamous histology.

3. Stage IIIB or IIIC NSCLC that is not amenable to curative surgery or definitive chemoradiation, or Stage IV NSCLC, according to the American Joint Committee on Cancer (AJCC) Cancer Staging Manual, 9th edition.

4. No prior systemic therapy for locally advanced or metastatic NSCLC. Prior neoadjuvant or adjuvant chemotherapy or chemoradiation is allowed if completed at least 12 months before randomization.

5. At least 1 measurable lesion per RECIST v1.1 as assessed by the investigator. A lesion in a previously irradiated field is measurable only if it has shown unequivocal progression since radiotherapy.

narrativeContentItems.name: NCI-55
narrativeContentItems.text:
6. PD-L1 TPS ≥1% determined by the central laboratory using the PD-L1 IHC 22C3 pharmDx assay on a tumor tissue sample (archival tissue obtained within 6 months before randomization without intervening systemic therapy, or a fresh biopsy).

7. Documented absence of epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) sensitizing mutations, anaplastic lymphoma kinase (ALK) and ROS1 rearrangements, and other genomic alterations for which an approved first-line targeted therapy is available locally (including BRAF V600E, RET fusions, MET exon 14 skipping, and NTRK fusions). Testing is required for nonsquamous histology and for squamous histology in participants who never smoked (Section 8.2).

narrativeContentItems.name: NCI-56
narrativeContentItems.text:
8. Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 0 or 1.

9. Life expectancy of at least 3 months.

10. Adequate organ function within 7 days before randomization: absolute neutrophil count ≥1.5 × 10⁹/L; platelets ≥100 × 10⁹/L; hemoglobin ≥9.0 g/dL without transfusion within 14 days; creatinine clearance ≥50 mL/min (Cockcroft-Gault); international normalized ratio (INR) and activated partial thromboplastin time ≤1.5 × upper limit of normal (ULN) unless receiving anticoagulant therapy; urine protein <2+ by dipstick or urine protein-to-creatinine ratio <1.0 g/g. Liver chemistry requirements are specified in Section 5.3.

narrativeContentItems.name: NCI-57
narrativeContentItems.text:
11. Male and female assigned at birth, inclusive of all gender identities.

Contraceptive use by participants should be consistent with local regulations regarding the methods of contraception for those participating in clinical studies.

Male participants: No contraceptive requirements apply. Drug A and Drug B are monoclonal antibodies without genotoxic potential, and seminal transfer is not expected to result in clinically relevant exposure of a partner.

Female participants:

A participant is eligible to participate if not pregnant or breastfeeding, and one of the following conditions applies:

  • Is of nonchildbearing potential (NCBP) as defined in Section 5.4.1.

OR

  • Is of childbearing potential (CBP) and using a contraceptive method that is highly effective (with a failure rate of < 1% per year), preferably with low user dependency, as described in Section 5.4.2 during the study intervention period and for at least 6 months after the last dose of study intervention. The investigator should evaluate the potential for contraceptive method failure (eg, noncompliance, recently initiated) in relationship to the first dose of study intervention.

A CBP participant must have a negative highly sensitive pregnancy test (serum, as required by local regulations) within 72 hours before the first dose of study intervention, see Section 8.4.5.

Additional requirements for pregnancy testing during and after study intervention are located in Section 8.4.5.

The investigator is responsible for review of medical history, menstrual history, and recent sexual activity where pregnancy can occur to decrease the risk for inclusion of a participant with an early undetected pregnancy.

narrativeContentItems.name: NCI-58
narrativeContentItems.text: 12. Signed informed consent as described in Section 11.1 which includes compliance with the requirements and restrictions listed in the informed consent form (ICF) and in this protocol.

narrativeContentItems.name: NCI-59
narrativeContentItems.text: An individual who meets any of the following criteria will be excluded from participation in this trial:

narrativeContentItems.name: NCI-60
narrativeContentItems.text:
1. Untreated or symptomatic central nervous system metastases or leptomeningeal disease. Participants with treated brain metastases are eligible if radiologically stable for at least 4 weeks and not requiring corticosteroids above 10 mg/day prednisone equivalent for at least 14 days before randomization.

2. Active autoimmune disease that required systemic treatment within the past 2 years. Replacement therapy (eg, thyroxine, insulin, or physiologic corticosteroids) is not considered systemic treatment.

3. History of noninfectious pneumonitis or interstitial lung disease that required corticosteroids, or current pneumonitis.

4. Lymphoma, leukemia, or any malignancy other than NSCLC within the past 5 years except for basal cell or squamous epithelial carcinomas of the skin that have been resected with no evidence of metastatic disease for 3 years

5. Significant allergies to humanized monoclonal antibodies

6. Symptomatic herpes zoster within 3 months prior to screening

7. Active infection requiring systemic therapy within 14 days before randomization, or known active tuberculosis.

8. Clinically significant cardiovascular disease within 6 months before randomization, including myocardial infarction, unstable angina, stroke or transient ischemic attack, or New York Heart Association Class III or IV heart failure.

9. QTc >450 msec for male participants or QTc >470 msec for female participants or QTc >480 msec in participants with bundle branch block. NOTE: The QTc is the QT interval corrected for heart rate according to Fridericia’s formula (QTcF). It is either machine-read or manually over-read.

10. Prior allogeneic tissue or solid organ transplant.

narrativeContentItems.name: NCI-61
narrativeContentItems.text:
11. Alanine aminotransferase (ALT) >3 × ULN or total bilirubin >1.5 × ULN, confirmed on repeat testing.

Up to 5.0 × ULN higher baseline ALT is allowed for participants with documented metastases / tumor infiltration, if such participants are eligible to participate in the study.

12. Has cirrhosis or current unstable liver or biliary disease per investigator assessment defined by the presence of ascites, encephalopathy, coagulopathy, hypoalbuminemia, esophageal/gastric varices, or persistent jaundice.

NOTE: Stable noncirrhotic chronic liver disease (including Gilbert’s syndrome or asymptomatic gallstones), hepatobiliary involvement of malignancy, or chronic stable HBV infection (in a participant for whom hepatitis D virus infection has been excluded) or chronic HCV infection is acceptable if the participant otherwise meets entry criteria.

13. Evidence of chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection with detectable viral load despite antiviral therapy with high resistance barrier.

14. Positive antibodies to hepatitis D virus (HDV), or detectable HBV DNA without nucleos(t)ide analog prophylaxis started more than 1 week before the first dose of study intervention (Section 6.1).

narrativeContentItems.name: NCI-62
narrativeContentItems.text:
15. Tumor invading or abutting major blood vessels (eg, pulmonary artery, superior vena cava), or tumor cavitation, on screening imaging.

16. Hemoptysis of at least 2.5 mL of bright red blood in a single episode within 3 months before randomization, or clinically significant bleeding from any site within 4 weeks before randomization.

17. Uncontrolled hypertension (systolic blood pressure >150 mmHg or diastolic blood pressure >100 mmHg despite antihypertensive therapy), or history of hypertensive crisis or hypertensive encephalopathy.

18. Arterial thromboembolic event within 6 months, or venous thromboembolic event within 3 months, before randomization.

19. Gastrointestinal perforation or fistula within 6 months, major surgery within 4 weeks, or a nonhealing wound or fracture.

narrativeContentItems.name: NCI-63
narrativeContentItems.text:
20. Prior therapy with any immune checkpoint inhibitor or any anti-angiogenic agent.

21. Live vaccine(s) within 1 month prior to screening, or plans to receive such vaccines during the study

22. Systemic corticosteroids above 10 mg/day prednisone equivalent or other immunosuppressive therapy within 14 days before randomization. Inhaled, topical, and intra-articular corticosteroids are permitted.

23. Radiotherapy within 2 weeks before randomization, or thoracic radiotherapy of more than 30 Gy within 6 months before randomization.

narrativeContentItems.name: NCI-64
narrativeContentItems.text: 24. Current enrollment OR past participation in another investigational study in which an investigational intervention (eg, drug, vaccine, invasive device) was administered within 28 days before planned first dose of study intervention in this clinical study.

narrativeContentItems.name: NCI-65
narrativeContentItems.text:
25. Known human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection with a CD4+ T-cell count below 350 cells/µL, a detectable viral load, or an acquired immunodeficiency syndrome-defining illness within the past 12 months (FDA 2020).

26. Sensitivity to any of the study interventions, or components thereof, or drug or other allergy that, in the opinion of the investigator or medical monitor, contraindicates participation in the study.

Childbearing Potential (CBP) Participants or Partners

Individuals in the following categories are considered CBP (fertile):

5. Following menarche

6. From the time of menarche until becoming postmenopausal unless permanently sterile (see below)

  • A postmenopausal state is defined as no menses for 12 months without an alternative medical cause.
  • A high follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) level in the postmenopausal range may be used to confirm a postmenopausal state in individuals not using hormonal contraception or hormonal replacement therapy (HRT). However, in the absence of 12 months of amenorrhea, confirmation with more than one FSH measurement (>40 IU/L or mIU/mL) is required.
  • Individuals on HRT and whose menopausal status is in doubt will be required to use one of the nonestrogen hormonal highly effective contraception methods if they wish to continue their HRT during the study. Otherwise, they must discontinue HRT to allow confirmation of postmenopausal status before study enrollment.
  • Permanent sterilization methods and gender-affirming procedures (for the purpose of this trial) include:
  • Documented hysterectomy
  • Documented bilateral salpingectomy
  • Documented bilateral oophorectomy
  • For individuals with permanent infertility due to an alternate medical cause other than the above, (eg, Mullerian agenesis, androgen insensitivity, gonadal dysgenesis), investigator discretion should be applied to determining study entry.

Note: Documentation can come from the site personnel’s review of the participant’s medical records, medical examination, or medical history interview.

  • If fertility is unclear (eg, amenorrhea in adolescents or athletes) and a menstrual cycle cannot be confirmed before first dose of study intervention, additional evaluation should be considered.

Individuals who do not meet the definition of CBP are considered of nonchildbearing potential (NCBP).

narrativeContentItems.name: NCI-69
narrativeContentItems.text: No lifestyle restrictions are required other than those described in Section 5.5.4.

narrativeContentItems.name: NCI-70
narrativeContentItems.text: No restrictions are required.

narrativeContentItems.name: NCI-71
narrativeContentItems.text: No restrictions are required.

narrativeContentItems.name: NCI-72
narrativeContentItems.text: No restrictions are required.

narrativeContentItems.name: NCI-73
narrativeContentItems.text:
• Participants will not receive live or live-attenuated vaccines from 1 month before screening until 90 days after the last dose of study intervention. Inactivated vaccines (eg, seasonal influenza and COVID-19 vaccines) are permitted.
  • Participants will refrain from donating blood or blood products during the study and for 6 months after the last dose of study intervention.

narrativeContentItems.name: NCI-74
narrativeContentItems.text:
A screen failure occurs when a participant who has consented to participate in the clinical study is not subsequently randomized. A minimal set of screen failure information is required to ensure transparent reporting of screen failure participants to meet the CONSORT publishing requirements and to respond to queries from regulatory authorities. Minimal information includes demography, screen failure details, eligibility criteria, and any SAE.

Individuals who do not meet the criteria for participation in this study (screen failure) may be rescreened. Rescreened participants should be assigned a new participant number for every screening/rescreening event.

Rescreening is permitted once per participant, after discussion with the medical monitor. Central PD-L1 results may be reused at rescreening; other screening assessments will be repeated if they fall outside the windows specified in the SoA (Section 1.3).

narrativeContentItems.name: NCI-75
narrativeContentItems.text: Randomization or the first dose of study intervention will be delayed, within the 28-day screening window, for any of the following: an acute infection requiring systemic therapy until resolved; palliative radiotherapy until at least 2 weeks after completion; blood pressure above the limits in Section 5.3 until controlled; or a transfusion-dependent hemoglobin value until stable without transfusion for 14 days. Participants who cannot be randomized within the screening window will be recorded as screen failures and may be rescreened as described in Section 5.6.

narrativeContentItems.name: NCI-76
narrativeContentItems.text: Participants will be recruited from the investigators’ clinical practices and referral networks. Study information will be posted on ClinicalTrials.gov, the EU Clinical Trials Information System, and other applicable registries. Any participant-facing recruitment materials will be approved by the IRB/IEC before use. Sites will be selected to include diverse patient populations, and enrollment of participants from underrepresented groups will be monitored against disease epidemiology.

narrativeContentItems.name: NCI-77
NCI-78
NCI-79
narrativeContentItems.text: Not applicable.

narrativeContentItems.name: NCI-80
narrativeContentItems.text: Drug A will be administered at 20 mg/kg by IV infusion over 30 minutes (-5/+10 minutes) through an in-line 0.2-µm filter. The dose will be calculated using the body weight on Cycle 1 Day 1 and recalculated only if body weight changes by 10% or more from that value. Premedication is not required for the first dose. Participants will be observed for at least 60 minutes after the first 2 infusions and for 30 minutes after subsequent infusions.

narrativeContentItems.name: NCI-81
narrativeContentItems.text: Drug B will be administered at 200 mg by IV infusion over 30 minutes (-5/+10 minutes) through an in-line 0.2-µm filter, consistent with the locally approved prescribing information. Because both interventions have the same infusion duration and volume, the blind is maintained. Observation periods are the same as for Drug A.

narrativeContentItems.name: NCI-82
narrativeContentItems.text: Participants with detectable HBV DNA at screening will start a nucleos(t)ide analog with a high barrier to resistance (entecavir or tenofovir) more than 1 week before the first dose of study intervention (Cohen 2024). Prophylaxis will continue during study intervention and for at least 12 months after the last dose, with HBV DNA and liver chemistries monitored monthly (Section 12.4).

narrativeContentItems.name: NCI-83
narrativeContentItems.text: The rationale for selection of the dose and regimen for each investigational trial intervention is presented in the Drug A and Drug B subsections below.

narrativeContentItems.name: NCI-84
narrativeContentItems.text: The Drug A dose of 20 mg/kg IV Q3W was selected on the basis of Phase 1 and Phase 2 data. Doses ≥10 mg/kg maintained >95% peripheral checkpoint receptor occupancy and complete suppression of the free angiogenic ligand throughout the dosing interval. Population PK modeling predicts that 20 mg/kg maintains trough concentrations above the target saturation concentration in >95% of patients, including those with high tumor burden or low serum albumin. Exposure-response analyses showed no increase in Grade ≥3 AEs between 10 and 30 mg/kg, and ORR was numerically higher at 20 mg/kg than at 10 mg/kg (48% vs 36%) (Investigator’s Brochure, Section 5.5).

narrativeContentItems.name: NCI-85
narrativeContentItems.text: Drug B will be administered at the approved dose of 200 mg IV Q3W for up to 35 cycles, consistent with the locally approved prescribing information.

narrativeContentItems.name: NCI-86
narrativeContentItems.text: Participants will receive Drug A 20 mg/kg or Drug B 200 mg by IV infusion on Day 1 of each 21-day cycle for up to 35 cycles; an unblinded pharmacist will prepare masked infusions of identical duration. Retreatment following a dose delay will be governed by the criteria in Section 6.3.1.

narrativeContentItems.name: NCI-87
narrativeContentItems.text:
After a dose delay, the participant must meet all of the following criteria to be eligible for retreatment:

  • AE resolved to Grade ≤1 or baseline (Grade ≤2 for endocrinopathies controlled with replacement therapy).
  • Corticosteroid dose reduced to ≤10 mg/day prednisone equivalent.
  • Blood pressure controlled (<150/100 mmHg) and urine protein <2 g/24 hours, where applicable.
  • No ongoing study intervention discontinuation criterion (Section 7.1).

narrativeContentItems.name: NCI-88
narrativeContentItems.text: Dose reductions of Drug A or Drug B are not permitted. Toxicity will be managed by dose delay, infusion interruption, or permanent discontinuation according to Sections 6.4 to 6.4 and Section 12. Because the arm is blinded, the same rules apply to both arms. If both an immune-mediated and an anti-angiogenic class cause are possible, the more conservative action will be taken. Liver events will also be assessed against the liver event stopping criteria (Section 7.1.1.1).

narrativeContentItems.name: NCI-89
narrativeContentItems.text: A dose may be delayed for up to 12 weeks from the last dose to allow recovery from toxicity, or for longer if needed to taper corticosteroids, after discussion with the medical monitor. Delays for reasons other than toxicity (eg, vacation, intercurrent illness) of up to 3 weeks are permitted. Subsequent cycles will be rescheduled from the date of the delayed dose. Delays longer than 12 weeks will result in permanent discontinuation unless the medical monitor agrees that the participant is deriving benefit.

narrativeContentItems.name: NCI-90
narrativeContentItems.text: Immune-mediated AEs will be managed according to the guidelines in Section 12, which are aligned with the American Society of Clinical Oncology (ASCO) and European Society for Medical Oncology (ESMO) recommendations (Schneider 2021; Brahmer 2021). In general, study intervention will be withheld for Grade 2 or 3 events and permanently discontinued for Grade 4 events, recurrent Grade 3 events, Grade 2 or higher pneumonitis that recurs, Grade 3 or higher myocarditis, or any event requiring more than 12 weeks to resolve. Systemic corticosteroids (prednisone 1 to 2 mg/kg/day or equivalent) will be started for Grade 2 or higher events and tapered over at least 4 weeks.

narrativeContentItems.name: NCI-92
narrativeContentItems.text: For Grade 1 reactions, the infusion rate will be reduced by 50% until resolution. For Grade 2 reactions, the infusion will be interrupted and restarted at 50% of the rate after resolution, and premedication with an antihistamine and acetaminophen will be given before subsequent infusions. For Grade 3 or 4 reactions, the infusion will be stopped, and study intervention will be permanently discontinued. Anaphylaxis will be managed according to institutional standards.

narrativeContentItems.name: NCI-93
narrativeContentItems.text:
For this study, any dose of Drug A or Drug B greater than 110% of the protocol-specified dose within a 24-hour time period will be considered an overdose.

Sponsor does not recommend specific treatment for an overdose.

In the event of an overdose, the investigator should:

  • Evaluate the participant to determine, in consultation with the medical monitor, if possible, whether study intervention should be interrupted.
  • Closely monitor the participant for any AE/SAE and laboratory abnormalities as medically appropriate and at least until the next scheduled follow-up.
  • Obtain a serum sample for PK analysis within 7 days from the date of the last dose of study intervention if requested by the medical monitor (determined on a case-by-case basis).
  • Document the quantity of the excess dose as well as the duration of the overdose.

narrativeContentItems.name: NCI-94
NCI-95
narrativeContentItems.text: Drug A and Drug B vials will be stored at 2°C to 8°C, protected from light, and will not be frozen or shaken. Infusions will be prepared by an unblinded pharmacist in 0.9% sodium chloride to the same total volume (250 mL) and dispensed in identical opaque infusion bags and line covers (Section 6.7.3). Diluted solutions may be stored for up to 24 hours at 2°C to 8°C, including infusion time.

narrativeContentItems.name: NCI-96
narrativeContentItems.text:
1. The investigator or designee must confirm appropriate conditions (eg, temperature) have been maintained during transit for all study intervention received, and any discrepancies are reported and resolved before use of the study intervention.

2. All study intervention must be stored in a secure, environmentally controlled, and monitored (manual or automated) area in accordance with the labeled storage conditions with access limited to the investigator and authorized site staff.

narrativeContentItems.name: NCI-97
narrativeContentItems.text:
1. Only participants randomized to study intervention may receive study intervention, and only authorized site staff may supply, prepare, or administer study intervention.

3. The investigator, institution, the head of the medical institution (where applicable), or authorized site staff is responsible for study intervention accountability, reconciliation, and record maintenance (ie, receipt, reconciliation, and final disposition records).

4. Further guidance and information for the final disposition of unused study interventions are provided in the Pharmacy Manual.

Assignment to Study Intervention

Study intervention will be dispensed at the study visits as summarized in the SoA.

narrativeContentItems.name: NCI-98
NCI-99
narrativeContentItems.text: Participants will be randomized in a 1:1 ratio to Drug A or Drug B after eligibility has been confirmed, within 3 days before Cycle 1 Day 1. Randomization will be stratified by PD-L1 TPS (1% to 49% vs ≥50%) and histology (squamous vs nonsquamous).

narrativeContentItems.name: NCI-100
narrativeContentItems.text: All participants will be centrally assigned to randomized study intervention using an interactive response technology (IRT). Before the study is initiated, the log-in information and directions for the IRT will be provided to each site.

narrativeContentItems.name: NCI-101
narrativeContentItems.text: This is a double-blind study in which participants, care providers, investigators, and outcomes assessors are blinded to study intervention. The IRT will be programmed with blind-breaking instructions.

narrativeContentItems.name: NCI-102
narrativeContentItems.text:
Participants will be randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to receive study intervention. Investigators will remain blinded to each participant’s assigned study intervention throughout the course of the study. To maintain this blind, an otherwise uninvolved third party will be responsible for the reconstitution and dispensation of all study intervention and will endeavor to ensure that there are no differences in time taken to dispense following randomization.

In the event of a quality assurance audit, the auditor(s) will be allowed access to unblinded study intervention records at the site(s) to verify that randomization/dispensing has been conducted accurately.

Drug A and Drug B concentrations and ADA results will not be reported to blinded personnel before unblinding of the study.

narrativeContentItems.name: NCI-103
narrativeContentItems.text:
In case of an emergency, the investigator has the sole responsibility for determining if unblinding of a participants’ intervention assignment is warranted. Participant safety must always be the first consideration in making such a determination. If the investigator decides that unblinding is warranted, the investigator may, at the investigator’s discretion, contact the sponsor to discuss the situation prior to unblinding a participant’s intervention assignment unless this could delay emergency treatment for the participant. If a participant’s intervention assignment is unblinded, the sponsor must be notified within 24 hours of this occurrence. The date and reason for the unblinding must be recorded.

Sponsor safety staff may unblind the intervention assignment for any participant with an SAE. If the SAE requires that an expedited regulatory report be sent to one or more regulatory agencies, a copy of the report, identifying the participant’s intervention assignment, may be sent to investigators in accordance with local regulations and/or sponsor policy.

Knowledge of the assigned intervention is not required to manage immune-mediated or anti-angiogenic class AEs, because the management guidelines in Section 6.4 apply to both arms.

narrativeContentItems.name: NCI-104
narrativeContentItems.text:
When participants are dosed at the site, they will receive study intervention directly from the investigator or designee, under medical supervision. The date and time of each dose administered in the clinic will be recorded in the source documents. The dose of study intervention and study participant identification will be confirmed at the time of dosing by a member of the study site staff other than the person administering the study intervention.

The start and stop times of each infusion, the volume administered, and any infusion interruption will be recorded.

narrativeContentItems.name: NCI-105
narrativeContentItems.text: HBV antiviral prophylaxis with entecavir or tenofovir is a noninvestigational background intervention for participants with detectable HBV DNA (see Section 6.1). Rescue therapy is addressed in Section 6.9.2.

narrativeContentItems.name: NCI-106
narrativeContentItems.text:
Participants with detectable HBV DNA at screening will receive HBV antiviral prophylaxis with a nucleos(t)ide analog with a high barrier to resistance: entecavir or tenofovir (disoproxil or alafenamide). Prophylaxis will be administered orally once daily at the dose specified in the locally approved prescribing information, starting more than 1 week before the first dose of study intervention and continuing during study intervention and for at least 12 months after the last dose. HBV DNA and liver chemistries will be monitored monthly (see Section 12.4).

HBV antiviral prophylaxis is a background intervention classified as a NIMP/AxMP and will be provided locally by the study site from commercial supply.

narrativeContentItems.name: NCI-107
narrativeContentItems.text: The study site will not supply rescue medication. Premedication and supportive care are described in Section 6.10.2.

narrativeContentItems.name: NCI-108
narrativeContentItems.text:
Any medication or vaccine (including over-the-counter or prescription medicines, recreational drugs, vitamins, and/or herbal supplements) that the participant is receiving at the time of enrollment or receives during the study must be recorded along with:

  • Reason for use
  • Dates of administration including start and end dates
  • Dosage information including dose and frequency

The medical monitor should be contacted if there are any questions regarding concomitant or prior therapy.

Concomitant medications will be recorded from 28 days before Cycle 1 Day 1 through 30 days after the last dose, and medications given to treat SAEs or immune-mediated AEs will be recorded through 90 days after the last dose.

narrativeContentItems.name: NCI-109
narrativeContentItems.text:
• Any other anticancer therapy, including chemotherapy, targeted therapy, immunotherapy, or investigational agents.
  • Live or live-attenuated vaccines (Section 5.5.4).
  • Systemic immunosuppressive therapy above 10 mg/day prednisone equivalent, except to manage AEs.
  • Antiplatelet therapy with more than 325 mg/day aspirin, or dual antiplatelet therapy, because of bleeding risk.
  • Herbal or traditional medicines with anticancer intent.

narrativeContentItems.name: NCI-110
narrativeContentItems.text: Supportive care consistent with institutional standards is permitted, including antiemetics, analgesics, antihypertensives, hormone replacement, bone-modifying agents (denosumab or bisphosphonates) for bone metastases, hematopoietic growth factors per guidelines, inactivated vaccines, and prophylactic or therapeutic low-molecular-weight heparin or direct oral anticoagulants. Systemic corticosteroids are permitted to treat AEs, as premedication for contrast allergy, and at physiologic replacement doses.

narrativeContentItems.name: NCI-111
narrativeContentItems.text: Palliative radiotherapy to a limited field (eg, painful bone lesion) is permitted, provided the lesion is not a target lesion and the need for radiotherapy does not reflect disease progression. Study intervention will be withheld from 1 week before to 1 week after radiotherapy. Thoracic radiotherapy requires discussion with the medical monitor.

narrativeContentItems.name: NCI-112
narrativeContentItems.text: After discontinuation of study intervention, subsequent anticancer therapy is at the investigator’s discretion. The regimen, start and stop dates, best response, and date of progression on that therapy will be recorded to support the PFS2 and OS analyses. Whenever possible, subsequent therapy will start after BICR-confirmed progression.

narrativeContentItems.name: NCI-113
NCI-114
NCI-115
narrativeContentItems.text: Liver event stopping criteria and QTc stopping criteria are described in Sections 7.1.1.1 and 7.1.1.2, respectively. Participants who permanently discontinue study intervention will complete end-of-treatment and safety follow-up visits and continue efficacy and survival follow-up unless they withdraw consent; see Section 1.3 for assessments at discontinuation and during follow-up.

narrativeContentItems.name: NCI-116
narrativeContentItems.text:
Discontinuation of study intervention for abnormal liver tests is required by the investigator when a participant meets one of the conditions outlined in the algorithm (Figure 2) or in the presence of abnormal liver chemistries not meeting protocol-specified stopping rules if the investigator believes that it is in best interest of the participant.

Study intervention will be discontinued for a participant if liver event criteria are met.

Figure 2. Phase 3-4 Liver Event Criteria Algorithm (Option A: ALT Only)

Refer to Section 12.4 Liver Safety: Suggested Actions, Monitoring, and Follow-up to Assess Causality of Liver Event. Participants who do not meet protocol specified liver event stopping criteria but met protocol defined increased monitoring criteria may continue study intervention with increased liver chemistry monitoring. Refer to Section 12.4 Liver Safety: Liver Event Increased Monitoring Criteria With Continued Study Intervention.

Immune-mediated hepatitis will also be managed according to Section 6.4 and Section 12; where the 2 sets of rules differ, the more conservative action will be taken.

narrativeContentItems.name: NCI-117
narrativeContentItems.text: If a clinically significant finding is identified (including, but not limited to, changes from baseline in QT interval corrected using Fridericia’s formula [QTcF]) after enrollment, the investigator or qualified designee will determine if the participant can continue on the study intervention and if any change in participant management is needed. This review of the ECG printed at the time of collection must be documented. Any new clinically relevant finding should be reported as an AE.

narrativeContentItems.name: NCI-118
narrativeContentItems.text: Study intervention may be temporarily withheld for toxicity or other reasons as described in Section 6.4. Participants who temporarily discontinue study intervention will continue all study assessments according to the SoA, including tumor imaging on the original schedule.

narrativeContentItems.name: NCI-119
narrativeContentItems.text: Rechallenge after an immune-mediated AE is permitted only as specified in Section 6.4 and Section 12. Rechallenge after any event requiring permanent discontinuation is not permitted, except as described in Section 7.1.3.1.

narrativeContentItems.name: NCI-120
narrativeContentItems.text:
Study intervention restart/rechallenge after liver chemistry stopping criteria are met is allowed in this study. If the participant meets liver chemistry stopping criteria, do not restart/rechallenge the participant with study intervention unless:

  • Sponsor Safety Review Board approval is granted
  • Ethics and/or IRB approval is obtained, if required, and
  • Separate consent for intervention restart/rechallenge is signed by the participant

NOTE: If study intervention was interrupted for suspected intervention-induced liver injury, the participant should be informed of the risk of death, liver transplantation, hospitalization, and jaundice and reconsented before resumption of dosing.

Refer to Section 12.4 Liver Safety: Suggestions and Guidelines for Liver Events for details on the restart/rechallenge process.

If Sponsor Safety Review Board approval to restart/rechallenge the participant with study intervention is not granted, then the participant must permanently discontinue study intervention and may continue in the study for protocol-specified follow-up assessments.

narrativeContentItems.name: NCI-121
narrativeContentItems.text:
In rare instances, it may be necessary for a participant to permanently discontinue study intervention. If study intervention is permanently discontinued, the participant should, if at all possible, remain in the study to be evaluated for disease progression (if study intervention was discontinued before progression), subsequent therapy, and survival. See the SoA for data to be collected at the time of discontinuation of study intervention and follow-up and for any further evaluations that need to be completed.

Study intervention will be permanently discontinued for any of the following:

  • Disease progression per RECIST v1.1 confirmed by BICR, unless the criteria for treatment beyond progression are met (Section 7.1).
  • Unacceptable toxicity, including AEs requiring permanent discontinuation (Section 6.4) or meeting liver event stopping criteria (Section 7.1.1.1).
  • Completion of 35 cycles of study intervention.
  • Pregnancy (Section 9.3.1).
  • Start of another anticancer therapy.
  • Participant decision or investigator decision that continuation is not in the participant’s best interest.

Participants who discontinue study intervention will complete the end-of-treatment and safety follow-up visits and will continue in efficacy and survival follow-up unless they withdraw consent.

narrativeContentItems.name: NCI-122
narrativeContentItems.text: Because immunotherapy may produce atypical responses, participants with initial BICR-confirmed progression may continue study intervention if all of the following apply: the investigator judges that the participant is deriving clinical benefit; ECOG performance status is stable; there is no rapid progression, progression at critical sites (eg, spinal cord compression) requiring urgent intervention, or unacceptable toxicity; and the participant signs a separate consent acknowledging alternative treatment options. Tumor imaging will continue per the SoA, and response will also be assessed per immune RECIST (iRECIST) (Seymour 2017). Study intervention will be discontinued if further progression of at least 10% in the sum of diameters, or new lesions, is confirmed at the next assessment. For all efficacy analyses, the first BICR-confirmed progression is the PFS event.

narrativeContentItems.name: NCI-123
narrativeContentItems.text:
• A participant may withdraw from the study at any time at the participant’s own request for any reason (or without providing any reason) without any negative consequences.
  • A participant may be withdrawn at any time at the discretion of the investigator for safety, behavioral, or compliance reasons.
  • At the time of discontinuing from the study, if possible, an early discontinuation visit should be conducted, as shown in the SoA. See SoA for data to be collected at the time of study discontinuation and follow-up and for any further evaluations that need to be completed.
  • The participant will be permanently discontinued from the study intervention and the study at that time.
  • If the participant withdraws consent for disclosure of future information, the sponsor may retain and continue to use any data collected before such a withdrawal of consent.
  • If a participant withdraws from the study, the participant may request destruction of any samples taken and not tested, and the investigator must document this in the site study records.

narrativeContentItems.name: NCI-124
narrativeContentItems.text:
A participant will be considered lost to follow-up if the participant repeatedly fails to return for scheduled visits and is unable to be contacted by the study site.

The following actions must be taken if a participant fails to return to the clinic for a required study visit:

  • The site must attempt to contact the participant and reschedule the missed visit as soon as possible, counsel the participant on the importance of maintaining the assigned visit schedule, and ascertain whether the participant wishes to and/or should continue in the study.
  • Before a participant is deemed lost to follow-up, the investigator or designee must make every effort to regain contact with the participant (where possible, 3 telephone calls, and if necessary, a certified letter to the participant’s last known mailing address or local equivalent methods). These contact attempts should be documented in the participant’s medical record.
  • Should the participant continue to be unreachable, the participant will be considered to have withdrawn from the study.
  • Site personnel, or an independent third party, will attempt to collect the vital status of the participant within legal and ethical boundaries for all participants randomized, including those who did not get study intervention. Public sources may be searched for vital status information. If vital status is determined as deceased, this will be documented and the participant will not be considered lost to follow-up. Sponsor personnel will not be involved in any attempts to collect vital status information.

narrativeContentItems.name: NCI-125
narrativeContentItems.text: Discontinuation of specific sites or of the study as a whole are detailed in Section 11.1.

narrativeContentItems.name: NCI-126
NCI-127
narrativeContentItems.text:
• Study procedures and their timing are summarized in the SoA. Protocol waivers or exemptions are not allowed.
  • Adherence to the study design requirements, including those specified in the SoA, is essential and required for study conduct.
  • All screening evaluations must be completed and reviewed to confirm that potential participants meet all eligibility criteria. The investigator will maintain a screening log to record details of all participants screened and to confirm eligibility or record reasons for screening failure, as applicable.
  • Procedures conducted as part of the participant’s routine clinical management (eg, blood count, imaging) and obtained before signing of the ICF may be utilized for screening or baseline purposes provided the procedures met the protocol-specified criteria and were performed within the timeframe defined in the SoA.
  • In the event of a significant study-continuity issue (eg, caused by a pandemic), alternate strategies for participant visits, assessments, medication distribution and monitoring may be implemented by the sponsor or the investigator, as per local health authority/ethics requirements.
  • PK, ADA, and biomarker results that could unblind the study will not be reported to investigative sites or other blinded personnel until the study has been unblinded.
  • Planned timepoints for all assessments are provided in the SoA.

The maximum amount of blood collected from each participant over the duration of the study, including any extra assessments that may be required, will not exceed 450 mL.

Repeat or unscheduled samples may be taken for safety reasons or for technical issues with the samples.

narrativeContentItems.name: NCI-128
narrativeContentItems.text: At screening, demography (age, sex, race, and ethnicity where permitted by local regulations), medical history, smoking history (pack-years and current or former status), NSCLC history (date of diagnosis, histology, stage, and prior therapies), and height will be recorded.

narrativeContentItems.name: NCI-129
narrativeContentItems.text: A formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded tumor tissue block or at least 15 unstained slides from a core needle, excisional, or incisional biopsy is required. Fine-needle aspirates, cytology specimens, and bone lesions are not acceptable. PD-L1 expression will be assessed by the central laboratory using the PD-L1 IHC 22C3 pharmDx assay, and the TPS will be reported to the IRT for eligibility and stratification. Remaining tissue will be used for the biomarker analyses in Section 8.6.3.

narrativeContentItems.name: NCI-130
narrativeContentItems.text: Results from a validated local test (tissue or plasma) performed before screening are acceptable for EGFR, ALK, ROS1, and other actionable alterations listed in Section 5.2. If local results are unavailable, testing will be performed centrally with a validated next-generation sequencing panel before randomization.

narrativeContentItems.name: NCI-131
narrativeContentItems.text: All participants will be tested at screening for hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg), hepatitis B core antibody (anti-HBc) total immunoglobulin, and antibody to hepatitis B surface antigen (anti-HBs) (Hwang 2020). Participants who are HBsAg-positive or anti-HBc-positive will have HBV DNA measured by a quantitative nucleic acid assay, and HBsAg-positive participants will be tested for antibodies to HDV. Hepatitis C antibody will be tested, with reflex HCV RNA if positive. Management is described in Section 6.1 and Section 12.4.

narrativeContentItems.name: NCI-132
narrativeContentItems.text: Efficacy assessments and procedures are described in the following subsections: Tumor Imaging and Assessment per RECIST v1.1, Blinded Independent Central Review, Survival Follow-up, and Patient-reported Outcomes (EORTC QLQ-C30 and QLQ-LC13). Assessment timepoints are provided in the SoA (Section 1.3).

narrativeContentItems.name: NCI-133
narrativeContentItems.text: Computed tomography (CT) with contrast of the chest and abdomen (and pelvis when clinically indicated) will be performed within 28 days before randomization, every 6 weeks (±7 days) from randomization through Week 48, and every 9 weeks (±7 days) thereafter until BICR-confirmed progression, start of new anticancer therapy, withdrawal of consent, or death. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) may be used if CT is contraindicated. Brain MRI is required at screening and thereafter as clinically indicated, or at each tumor assessment for participants with brain metastases at baseline. The same imaging modality and technique will be used throughout the study. Imaging will continue on the calendar schedule regardless of dose delays. Investigators will assess response per RECIST v1.1 (Eisenhauer 2009), and per iRECIST (Seymour 2017) for participants treated beyond progression.

narrativeContentItems.name: NCI-134
narrativeContentItems.text: All images will be submitted to the BICR on an ongoing basis. The BICR will consist of 2 independent radiologists, with adjudication by a third radiologist when needed, who are blinded to intervention assignment and investigator assessments. When the investigator assesses progression, the site will request expedited BICR review; the BICR result will be returned within 5 business days. Study intervention will continue during this period if clinically appropriate.

narrativeContentItems.name: NCI-135
narrativeContentItems.text: After discontinuation of study intervention, survival status and subsequent anticancer therapy will be collected every 12 weeks (±14 days) by clinic visit or telephone contact until death, withdrawal of consent, or end of study. Additional survival sweeps will be performed before each analysis of OS.

narrativeContentItems.name: NCI-136
narrativeContentItems.text: The EORTC QLQ-C30 and QLQ-LC13 will be completed electronically by the participant at the clinic before any other study procedure and before discussion of results, at the timepoints in the SoA. Deterioration is defined as an increase of at least 10 points from baseline in the cough, chest pain, or dyspnea scales, confirmed at the next assessment. Site staff will review questionnaires for completeness but not influence responses. Scores will be derived according to the EORTC scoring manual (Fayers 2001).

narrativeContentItems.name: NCI-137
narrativeContentItems.text: Planned timepoints for all safety assessments are provided in the SoA (Section 1.3).

narrativeContentItems.name: NCI-138
narrativeContentItems.text:
• A complete physical examination will include, at a minimum, assessments of the general appearance, skin, head and neck, lymph nodes, cardiovascular, respiratory, gastrointestinal, musculoskeletal, and neurological systems. Height and weight will also be measured and recorded.
  • A brief physical examination will include, at a minimum, assessments of the skin, lungs, cardiovascular system, and abdomen (liver and spleen), and any symptom-directed systems.
  • Investigators should pay special attention to clinical signs related to previous serious illnesses.

narrativeContentItems.name: NCI-139
narrativeContentItems.text:
• Oral, tympanic, axillary, or temporal artery temperature, pulse rate, respiratory rate, and blood pressure will be recorded (before blood collection for laboratory tests).
  • Blood pressure and pulse measurements will be assessed in a seated position with a completely automated device. Manual techniques will be used only if an automated device is not available.
  • Blood pressure and pulse measurements should be preceded by at least 5 minutes of rest for the participant in a quiet setting without distractions (eg, television, cell phones).

Blood pressure will be measured before and within 30 minutes after the end of each infusion. Weight will be measured on Day 1 of each cycle for dose calculation (Section 6.1).

narrativeContentItems.name: NCI-140
narrativeContentItems.text: • Single 12-lead ECG(s) will be obtained as outlined in the SoA (see Section 1.3) using an ECG machine that automatically calculates the heart rate and measures PR, QRS, QT, and QTcF intervals. Refer to Section 7.1.1.2 for QTcF withdrawal criteria and any additional QTcF readings that may be necessary.

narrativeContentItems.text:

  • The investigator must review the laboratory results, document this review, and record any clinically significant changes occurring during the study as an AE. The laboratory results must be retained with source documents.
  • Abnormal laboratory findings associated with the underlying disease are not considered clinically significant unless judged by the investigator to be more severe than expected for the participant’s condition.
  • All laboratory tests with values considered clinically significantly abnormal during participation in the study or within 90 days after the last dose of study intervention should be repeated until the values return to normal or baseline or are no longer considered clinically significant by the investigator or medical monitor.

0. If clinically significant values do not return to normal/baseline within a period of time judged reasonable by the investigator, the etiology should be identified, and the sponsor notified.

0. If laboratory values from non-protocol-specified laboratory tests performed at the institution’s local laboratory require a change in participant management or are considered clinically significant by the investigator (eg, SAE or AE or dose modification), then the results must be recorded.

narrativeContentItems.name: NCI-142
narrativeContentItems.text:
• Refer to Section 5.2 for pregnancy testing entry criteria.
  • Pregnancy testing (urine or serum as required by local regulations) should be conducted at monthly intervals during study intervention.
  • Pregnancy testing (urine or serum as required by local regulations) should be conducted at the end of relevant systemic exposure and correspond with the time frame for female participant contraception in Section 5.2.
  • Additional serum or urine pregnancy tests may be performed, as determined necessary by the investigator or required by local regulation, to establish the absence of pregnancy at any time during the participant’s participation in the study.

Monthly testing will be performed with the Day 1 laboratory tests of each cycle; serum testing is required at screening, and urine or serum testing thereafter. The test at the end of relevant systemic exposure will be performed 6 months after the last dose.

narrativeContentItems.name: NCI-143
narrativeContentItems.text: Not applicable.

narrativeContentItems.name: NCI-144
narrativeContentItems.text: ALT, aspartate aminotransferase, alkaline phosphatase, and total bilirubin will be measured on Day 1 of each cycle. Participants who meet the increased monitoring criteria (Section 12.4) will have liver chemistries measured weekly until they resolve, normalize, or return to baseline. Participants receiving HBV prophylaxis or with positive anti-HBc at baseline will have HBV DNA measured monthly (Section 12.4).

narrativeContentItems.name: NCI-145
narrativeContentItems.text: ECOG performance status will be assessed by the investigator or a qualified designee at the timepoints in the SoA, before study intervention administration, using the scale in Section 12. Whenever possible, the same assessor will evaluate a participant throughout the study. A performance status of 0 or 1 is required for eligibility (Section 5.2), and stability of performance status is a condition for treatment beyond progression (Section 7.1).

narrativeContentItems.name: NCI-146
narrativeContentItems.text:
• Serum samples of approximately 3.5 mL will be collected for measurement of serum concentrations of Drug A and Drug B as specified in the SoA (Section 1.3).
  • A maximum of 3 samples may be collected at additional timepoints during the study if warranted and agreed upon between the investigator and the sponsor. The timing of sampling may be altered during the course of the study based on newly available data (eg, to obtain data closer to the time of peak plasma concentrations) to ensure appropriate monitoring.
  • Instructions for the collection and handling of biological samples will be provided by the sponsor. The actual date and time (24-hour clock time) of each sample will be recorded.
  • Samples will be used to evaluate the PK of Drug A and Drug B. Each serum sample will be divided into 2 aliquots (1 each for PK and a backup). Samples collected for analyses of study intervention (serum) concentration may also be used to evaluate safety or efficacy aspects related to concerns arising during or after the study.
  • Genetic analyses will not be performed on these serum samples unless consent for this was included in the informed consent. Participant confidentiality will be maintained. At visits during which serum samples for the determination of PK and immunogenicity of Drug A and Drug B will be taken, one sample of sufficient volume can be used.
  • Intervention concentration information that would unblind the study will not be reported to investigative sites or blinded personnel until the study has been unblinded.

Drug B samples will be collected and stored to maintain the blind and may be analyzed to support exposure comparisons. Population PK and exposure-response analyses of Drug A will be described in a separate analysis plan.

narrativeContentItems.name: NCI-149
narrativeContentItems.text: Free and total concentrations of the angiogenic target ligand will be measured in the serum PK samples from participants receiving Drug A as an exploratory pharmacodynamic marker of target engagement. No additional samples are required.

narrativeContentItems.name: NCI-150
narrativeContentItems.text: • The Sponsor may store samples for up to 15 years after the end of the study to achieve study objectives. Additionally, with participants’ consent, samples may be used for further research by the Sponsor or others such as universities or other companies to contribute to the understanding of lung cancer or other diseases, the development of related or new treatments, or research methods.

narrativeContentItems.name: NCI-151
narrativeContentItems.text:
• Tumor tissue samples will be collected to explore tumor biomarkers associated with response and resistance to Drug A. Biomarkers will include PD-L1 expression levels, CD8+ T-cell infiltration, microvessel density, tumor mutational burden, and gene expression signatures. Samples will be collected according to the schedule described in the SoA and as detailed in the laboratory manual provided separately to sites.

An optional on-treatment or progression biopsy may be collected from participants who provide separate consent, when the investigator judges it safe.

narrativeContentItems.name: NCI-152
narrativeContentItems.text: • Plasma samples will be collected to evaluate ctDNA dynamics as an early marker of response and to characterize genomic mechanisms of resistance. Biomarkers will include ctDNA variant allele fraction and acquired genomic alterations. Samples will be collected according to the schedule described in the SoA and as detailed in the laboratory manual provided separately to sites.

narrativeContentItems.name: NCI-153
narrativeContentItems.text:
Antibodies to Drug A will be evaluated in serum samples collected from all participants according to the SoA. Additionally, serum samples should also be collected at the final visit from participants who discontinued study intervention or were withdrawn from the study. These samples will be tested by the sponsor or sponsor’s designee.

Serum samples will be screened for antibodies binding to Drug A and the titer of confirmed positive samples will be reported. Other analyses may be performed to verify the stability of antibodies to Drug A and/or further characterize the immunogenicity of Drug A.

The detection and characterization of antibodies to Drug A will be performed using a validated assay method by or under the supervision of the sponsor. All samples collected for detection of antibodies to Drug A will also be evaluated for Drug A serum concentration to enable interpretation of the antibody data. Antibodies may be further characterized and/or evaluated for their ability to neutralize the activity of the study intervention(s). Samples may be stored for a maximum of 15 years (or according to local regulations) following the last participant’s last visit for the study at a facility selected by the sponsor to enable further analysis of immune responses to Drug A.

Samples from participants receiving Drug B will be collected to maintain the blind; ADA testing for Drug B is not planned.

narrativeContentItems.name: NCI-154
narrativeContentItems.text:
For all participants throughout the study, the investigator and study site personnel will collect data about health care resource utilization associated with medical encounters.

The data collected will

  • Include the reasons and duration of hospitalizations and emergency room visits and
  • Exclude procedures, tests, and encounters mandated by the protocol.

The sponsor may use the collected data to conduct economic analyses.

narrativeContentItems.name: NCI-155
narrativeContentItems.text:
The definitions of adverse events (AEs) and serious adverse events (SAEs) can be found in Section 9.1.

The investigator and any qualified designees are responsible for detecting, documenting, and recording events that meet the definition of an AE or SAE and remain responsible for following up AEs that are serious, considered related to the study intervention or study procedures, or that caused the participant to discontinue the study intervention (see Section 7). This includes events reported by the participant (or, when appropriate, by a caregiver, surrogate, or the participant’s legally authorized representative).

The method of recording, evaluating, and assessing causality of AEs and SAEs and the procedures for completing and transmitting SAE reports are provided in Section 9.1.

narrativeContentItems.name: NCI-156
NCI-157
narrativeContentItems.text:
AE Definition

  • An AE is any untoward medical occurrence in a clinical study participant, temporally associated with the use of study intervention, whether or not considered related to the study intervention.
  • NOTE: An AE can therefore be any unfavorable and unintended sign (including an abnormal laboratory finding), symptom, or disease (new or exacerbated) temporally associated with the use of study intervention.

Events Meeting the AE Definition

  • Any abnormal laboratory test results (hematology, clinical chemistry, or urinalysis) or other safety assessments (eg, ECG, radiological scans, vital signs measurements), including those that worsen from baseline, considered clinically significant in the medical and scientific judgment of the investigator (ie, not related to progression of underlying disease, or more severe than expected for the participant’s condition)
  • Exacerbation of a chronic or intermittent pre-existing condition including either an increase in frequency and/or intensity of the condition
  • New condition detected or diagnosed after study intervention administration even though it may have been present before the start of the study.
  • Signs, symptoms, or the clinical sequelae of a suspected drug-drug interaction
  • Signs, symptoms, or the clinical sequelae of a suspected overdose of either study intervention or a concomitant medication. Overdose per se will not be reported as an AE/SAE unless it is an intentional overdose taken with possible suicidal/self-harming intent. Such overdoses should be reported regardless of sequelae.
  • Lack of efficacy or failure of expected pharmacological action per se will not be reported as an AE or SAE. Such instances will be captured in the efficacy assessments. However, the signs, symptoms, and/or clinical sequelae resulting from lack of efficacy will be reported as AE or SAE if they fulfill the definition of an AE or SAE.

Events not Meeting the AE Definition

  • Any abnormal laboratory findings or other abnormal safety assessments that are associated with the underlying disease, unless judged by the investigator to be more severe than expected for the participant’s condition.
  • The disease/disorder being studied or expected progression, signs, or symptoms of the disease/disorder being studied, unless more severe than expected for the participant’s condition.
  • Medical or surgical procedure (eg, endoscopy, appendectomy): the condition that leads to the procedure is the AE.
  • Situations in which an untoward medical occurrence did not occur (social and/or convenience admission to a hospital).
  • Anticipated day-to-day fluctuations of pre-existing disease(s) or condition(s) present or detected at the start of the study that do not worsen.

narrativeContentItems.name: NCI-158
narrativeContentItems.text:
An SAE is defined as any untoward medical occurrence that, at any dose, meets one or more of the criteria listed:

a. Results in death

a. Is life threatening

The term life threatening in the definition of serious refers to an event in which the participant was at risk of death at the time of the event. It does not refer to an event, which hypothetically might have caused death, if it were more severe.

b. Requires inpatient hospitalization or prolongation of existing hospitalization

  • In general, hospitalization signifies that the participant has been admitted (usually involving at least an overnight stay) at the hospital or emergency ward for observation and/or treatment that would not have been appropriate in the physician’s office or outpatient setting. Complications that occur during hospitalization are AEs. If a complication prolongs hospitalization or fulfills any other serious criteria, the event is serious. When in doubt as to whether hospitalization occurred or was necessary, the AE should be considered serious.
  • Hospitalization for elective treatment of a pre-existing condition that did not worsen from baseline is not considered an AE.

c. Results in persistent or significant disability/incapacity

  • The term disability means a substantial disruption of a person’s ability to conduct normal life functions.
  • This definition is not intended to include experiences of relatively minor medical significance such as uncomplicated headache, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, influenza, and accidental trauma (eg, sprained ankle) that may interfere with or prevent everyday life functions but do not constitute a substantial disruption.

d. Is a congenital anomaly/birth defect

e. Is a suspected transmission of any infectious agent via an authorized medicinal product

f. Other situations:

  • Medical or scientific judgment should be exercised by the investigator in deciding whether SAE reporting is appropriate in other situations such as important medical events that that may not be immediately life-threatening or result in death or hospitalization but may jeopardize the participant or may require medical or surgical intervention to prevent one of the other outcomes listed in the above definition. These events should usually be considered serious.
    • Examples of such events include invasive or malignant cancers, intensive treatment in an emergency room or at home for allergic bronchospasm, blood dyscrasias, convulsions not resulting in hospitalization, or development of intervention dependency or intervention abuse.
